chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Hisham ibn Salim and Hammad ibn Uthman and others — they said: We heard Abu Abdullah (AS) saying:

My hadith is the hadith of my father, and the hadith of my father is the hadith of my grandfather, and the hadith of my grandfather is the hadith of al-Husayn (AS), and the hadith of al-Husayn is the hadith of al-Hasan (AS), and the hadith of al-Hasan is the hadith of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS), and the hadith of Amir al-Mu'minin is the hadith of the Messenger of God (SAWW), and the hadith of the Messenger of God is the word of God, Mighty and Majestic.

key_terms.أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful — honorific title of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS)
key_terms.حَدِيثِي: my hadith — the Imam's transmitted narration, itself carrying divine authority
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic — a paired honorific of God indicating His absolute power and transcendence
key_terms.قَوْلُ اللَّهِ: the Word of God — divine speech; the ultimate, unmediated source of all Imamic narration

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about the chain of authority linking his hadith back to the word of God?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) establishes an unbroken chain of transmission ascending through each Imam — from himself, through al-Husayn (AS) and al-Hasan (AS), to Amir al-Mu'minin (AS), to the Prophet (SAWW) — and ultimately to the divine word of God Himself. This is a foundational creedal statement affirming that the Imams' teachings carry the same divine authority as revelation, since their speech traces back without interruption to God's own speech.
